context:
Terms read in full from the live vendor pages on 2026-10-22 and recorded in the ADR's 'Terms check' section. The readings come from the agreements themselves, not legal advice. Related: trial-capacity-disclosure-bundles-20261006 covers trial capacity SKUs, not these conditions.

Revalidated 2026-11-11 (origin/develop c7b75c80bc): still required, no condition is checked or documented as a publishing step yet. PR #3266 is merged (2026-10-22). The ADR now lives at docs/development/adr/adr-client-link-locality-disclosure.md in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site, not in the core repo, so the link is stale. The only related hook in core is the funding-source disclosure (FUNDING_SOURCES includes "free-trial", benchbox/validation/bundle.py:47 and core/results/provenance.py:42); there is no plan-tier or preview-feature field in bundles and no validator check for free, trial or preview tiers. Live cloud runs are not approved, so the live-cloud publish step of the acceptance cannot be exercised yet; the documented checklist and bundle fields can be built without live runs.

2026-11-12: Merged in PR #4137 (f4ffb30eaf, 2026-11-12) with benchbox-site PR #140. Core side delivered: submission manifests record plan tier, preview features, vendor permission, vendor notice and self-run attestation; the validator and benchbox submit refuse free-tier, trial and preview results without vendor permission and warn when a notice condition is not recorded. Remaining: the documented per-vendor publishing checklist in site docs, and applying it at the first live-cloud publication (live cloud is 'not now').

2026-11-12: benchbox-site PR #149 (7477d9a868, merged 2026-11-12) adds docs/vendor-publishing-checklist.md: for BigQuery, Redshift/Athena, Snowflake, Databricks, ClickHouse Cloud, MotherDuck and Starburst Galaxy, every ADR Terms-check condition is mapped to a manifest field / benchbox submit option / validator refusal (evaluate_vendor_conditions in benchbox/validation/bundle.py) or a documented manual step; linked from the ADR and docs/contributing-results.md. Manual-only conditions: reciprocity; replication info sent to vendor and Snowflake advance sharing (vendor_notice only warns when missing); BigQuery hyperscaler consent (self_run attestation); preview/beta approval cannot be cross-checked against what the run used. Gap: a recorded vendor_permission lets a Databricks Beta result through the validator although the ADR treats Beta as excluded; the checklist tells publishers not to publish Beta results. Remaining: apply the checklist at the first live-cloud publication (live cloud not approved).

2026-11-12: BenchBox PR #4189 (merged 2026-11-12): evaluate_vendor_conditions refuses Databricks results declaring any Beta/Preview feature even with vendor_permission (ADR Terms check: 'Beta services excluded', no override), including platform variants; benchbox submit uses the same function. benchbox-site PR #150 (93d72130a6) updates the checklist to match. Note: site #149 and #150 landed on main although they describe unreleased core behaviour (v0.5.0 pin); next does not yet contain them because main has not been merged into next (the repo allows squash merges only). Remaining: apply the checklist at the first live-cloud publication.
description:
The locality ADR's terms table (read from each vendor's live terms, #3266) lists conditions on publishing benchmark results that nothing in BenchBox checks today:

- Snowflake: share results with Snowflake reasonably in advance of publishing (Acceptable Use Policy §IV).
- AWS (Redshift, Athena), ClickHouse Cloud and MotherDuck: send the replication information to the vendor, not only publish it (AWS Service Terms §1.8, ClickHouse AUP §2, MotherDuck MSA §1.5).
- Free, trial and preview tiers: do not publish results from Databricks Free Edition (needs express permission), MotherDuck free or trial use, or any Beta or Preview feature on AWS, Snowflake, Databricks or ClickHouse without the vendor's approval.
- BigQuery: only tests the publisher runs itself, not on behalf of a hyperscale cloud provider.

Decide how each condition is met (publishing checklist, bundle metadata such as the plan tier and preview features used, or a submission validator check), then implement it.
